title: Are you Growing Free or Getting Stuck?
author: Cindy Chance
summary: Cindy Chance, an executive coach and ethicist, argues that as we age we either get more stuck or more free, and that people often become a more extreme version of what they already were. She says friends who seem to have gone crazy in middle age are usually doubling down on strategies that once worked while ignoring consequences. When a blind spot meets life, people either rage at the world or do the hard work of changing themselves. Chance maps predictable stages, the treadmill of the thirties and forties, the reckoning of the fifties and sixties, and the question of what matters now in the seventies and beyond, each with its own questions. Her counsel is to build range and openness, name blind spots, try things you are bad at, and keep someone close who tells you the truth.
points: Age does not make anyone wiser by itself; experience is raw material, and what counts is what we let it open us to.
Habits wear a path like walking the same line through soft soil, and the ground on either side grows over until another way is unimaginable.
Blind spots tend to trigger an avalanche of consequences, after which a person either rages at the world or changes in a fundamental way.
Each life stage carries its own diagnostic questions, such as what daily choices are making of me, what I have been defending, and what I can put down.
Change requires a witness: someone who can listen without rushing to explain you and who loves you enough to tell you the truth.
quotes: As we live, we either get more stuck or we get more free. Whatever the circumstances, those are the choices.
Usually they are not so much crazy as a more extreme version of whatever they were before. As people get older, they can get more brittle.
They either 1) rage at the world or 2) do the hard work to understand what is going on, which inevitably leads to the conclusion that they must change themselves in some fundamental way.
Every grind comes with habits, and habits wear a path, like walking the same line through soft soil day after day. Once the path is worn, why leave it?
You don’t have to abandon the life you’ve lived to admit it has brought you somewhere new. You do have to hold your identity more loosely.
Getting older doesn’t make anyone wiser. Experience is raw material. What counts is what we let it open us to.
None of us does this alone. We need someone who can hear us without rushing to explain us, and someone who loves us enough to tell us the truth.
